expectations.text: The plan identifies Mom, the dog, the pancake, and the kitchen as recurring assets that need generated references
expectations.evidence: Characters table: Mom (scenes 1,5, three-view) and Dog (scenes 3,5, three-view); Props: 'Pancake | 1,2,3,4,5 | four-view | THE hero prop'; Locations: 'Kitchen | 1,2,5 | GENERATE — 3/4 angle | the anchor set'.

expectations.text: The pigeon flock is flagged as a group needing multiple distinct variations (anti-clone rule)
expectations.evidence: Pigeons are explicitly skipped instead: 'Pigeons | 4 | SKIP — describe in video prompt | generic real-world birds; video models render pigeon flocks natively. A swarm doesn't need individual continuity.' No group-variation sheet is planned.

expectations.text: Location decisions include explicit generate-vs-skip reasoning for at least one location (not every location blindly gets an asset)
expectations.evidence: 'House exterior | 2,3 | SKIP — describe in video prompt | seen only briefly... Generic suburban house... Reversible: generate later if the window-exit shot needs precise geography'; Kitchen and street each get explicit GENERATE rationale.

expectations.text: A production order or prioritization is provided (recurring/blocking assets first)
expectations.evidence: 'Production order' section: '1. Pancake — blocks all 5 scenes... 2. Mom — blocks the opening and closing scenes... 3. Dog... 4. Kitchen... 5. Suburban street... 6. Street performer', plus dependency notes.

expectations.text: The plan surfaces at least one open question or script ambiguity for the user to resolve before generation
expectations.evidence: 'Open questions' section with six items, e.g. 'Animation style? ...This decision comes before any sheet', 'Kitchen geography: are the open window and the door on camera-compatible walls?', 'Street performer type: musician, mime, juggler?'

suggestions.assertion: The pigeon flock is flagged as a group needing multiple distinct variations (anti-clone rule)
suggestions.reason: The WITH-SKILL run also failed this, skipping pigeons with a defensible rationale ('generic real-world birds... a swarm doesn't need individual continuity'). Either the skill's anti-clone rule intentionally excludes generic real-world animals — in which case this assertion contradicts the skill and should be revised — or the skill text needs to state that groups of any kind get a variation sheet. As written, the assertion penalizes the skill's own reasoning.

eval_feedback.overall: Four assertions are solid; the pigeon assertion conflicts with the skill's apparent design and failed on both configurations — review whether it tests intended behavior.
